steps.message:
Dale's comment G-4 wants freeboard dimensioning, sizing calculations and apron details for the emergency spillway on C-9. Before I put the drainage lead on it I need to know whether the spillway as drawn holds up. Work it against the improvement plans and the QA/QC checklist in Design-Drafting, the master drainage study and the storm drain worksheets in Reports-Studies, and the Phase 2 comments and the flood control district acceptance letter in Correspondence/Agency. Tell me whether we can answer G-4 with what's on the sheet today and whether the revisions trigger an amendment to the accepted master study, what the spillway detail and the basin notes have to say on the revised C-9, and where the overflow ends up once it leaves the berm. Put it in a memo to Callaway for my signature, dated 10/31/2026.

Save it as /filesystem/Memo_to_Callaway_Spillway_2026-10-31.docx. Commit to one disposition on each question rather than giving me options. Put units on every value and name the record it comes from. Do not round intermediate values. Work to professional engineering standards.

Yours was approved 03/14/2022, so the base clock runs to 03/14/2026 — but the statute also allows a two-year extension on top of that, so effectively you're covered out to 03/14/2028. That's a comfortable window.

Bottom line: you've got plenty of runway on the entitlement side. I wouldn't sweat the December recordation date from a TM standpoint — the tentative is the thing that has to stay alive, and by my read it's alive well into '28. Obviously your land-use counsel is the one to sign off on that, but from where I sit on the title side I'm not seeing any exposure that would make me want to rush anyone.

PRECONSTRUCTION MEETING — MEETING NOTES
Meeting date:  03/28/2023
Time:  9:00 a.m. – 11:15 a.m.
Location:  Project site trailer, Desert Sage Ranch, Rainbow Blvd. & Windmill Ln., Las Vegas, NV 89178
Called by:  Callaway Land Partners
Chair:  Garrett Nokes, Callaway Land Partners
Notes prepared by:  Max Braddock, Project Manager, Sundial Engineering & Survey
Notes finalized and distributed:  06/14/2023 (incorporating CCFD approval letter dated 06/12/2023, received after the meeting)
1.  Attendees
Distribution of these notes: attendees above, plus CCFD Fire Plans Examiner (Capt. Emmett Roark) and Sundial project file 2201-03.
2.  County Submittal and Inspection Sequence
The construction inspection sequence was walked through by Terrence Kolb (Clark County Public Works — Development Review). The following items were agreed and will govern Phase 2 inspection administration:
2.1  Inspection request procedure.
Mesquite Basin will submit inspection requests through the County Public Works construction inspection portal not less than 48 hours in advance of the requested inspection window. Requests will cite the improvement plan sheet, station range, and item to be inspected. Sundial's field engineer will be copied on each request; where the field engineer's presence is required (e.g., subgrade acceptance, storm drain pressure test, pavement structural section) Sundial will attend jointly with the County inspector.
2.2  Progressive inspections during construction.
Phase 2 will be inspected on a rolling basis by item: rough grading and moisture-density; storm drain trench, bedding and pressure tests prior to backfill; curb-and-gutter forming; subbase; base; and pavement placement. County inspector will sign each item on County inspection form; Sundial will maintain the running set of signed reports in the construction record for Phase 2.
2.3  Pre-final inspection.
When the improvements listed on the approved plans are complete in the field — including punch-list-condition landscape, signing and striping, and the temporary construction stub at the north boundary as shown on the improvement plans — Callaway will submit a written request for pre-final inspection. County will schedule the pre-final walk within ten (10) working days of the request. Sundial and Mesquite Basin will attend. Any punch items identified will be logged on the County form on-site and returned to Callaway the same week.
2.4  Final inspection and acceptance.
Following completion of pre-final punch, Callaway will submit a written request for final inspection with a signed contractor statement that punch items are complete. County will schedule final inspection within ten (10) working days. On satisfactory final inspection, County Public Works will issue a written improvement acceptance letter under separate cover. It was noted that Phase 2 offsite improvements (Rainbow Blvd. frontage, curb return at Windmill Ln., traffic control device) may be finalled and accepted on a schedule independent of the onsite balance; the two acceptances will be handled as separate letters. This is consistent with the release provisions in the Phase 2 improvement agreement and performance bond.
2.5  Record drawings.
Sundial will prepare Phase 2 record drawings (as-builts) from contractor red-lines, field survey, and County inspection reports, for submission with the improvement acceptance package. Sundial will maintain a working red-line set at the trailer for the duration of construction; the general contractor will keep a mirrored set. Record drawings will be sealed and dated after final inspection.
3.  Traffic Control and Access
3.1  Construction access — primary.
Primary construction ingress and egress for Phase 2 will be from Rainbow Blvd. at the approved Phase 2 entry throat. All haul routes into and out of the site will use this entry. A traffic control plan conforming to the MUTCD and Clark County Public Works standards has been submitted by Mesquite Basin and approved for the Rainbow Blvd. work zone (curb return, taper, and flagger station).
3.2  Temporary construction stub across undeveloped Phase 3.
A temporary construction stub will be graded and paved across the northern boundary of the built Phase 2 area, extending into and across the presently undeveloped Phase 3 parcel to tie back to Windmill Ln. This stub is called out on the approved improvement plans and shown on the traffic control exhibit distributed at the meeting.
Two uses of the stub were confirmed and agreed:
Construction traffic.  The stub will serve as a secondary construction access for material deliveries and heavy equipment during Phase 2 construction, relieving the Rainbow Blvd. entry.
Secondary emergency access for occupied Phase 2.  Once dwelling units in Phase 2 are occupied and while Phase 3 remains undeveloped ground, the stub will serve as the secondary point of access required by CCFD for Phase 2 emergency response.
Both uses are expressly temporary. The stub crosses ground that is planned for Phase 3 subdivision development. It exists only because the Phase 3 remainder is presently ungraded and open. When Phase 3 is developed the stub will be removed and superseded by whatever access configuration is approved for Phase 3 on its own merits. This limitation was discussed in the meeting and was subsequently confirmed in writing by CCFD.
CCFD approval status.
At the time of the meeting, the CCFD access approval for Phase 2 was under review. Following the meeting, CCFD issued its formal approval by letter dated 06/12/2023 (Capt. Emmett Roark, Fire Plans Examiner). The letter approves the secondary access configuration for Phase 2 as a temporary condition pending development of Phase 3. That temporary designation is acknowledged on the record. Callaway and Sundial will maintain the CCFD letter in the project record and will treat the stub as a Phase 2 arrangement only; nothing in the CCFD Phase 2 correspondence is to be read as approval of an access configuration for Phase 3.
3.3  Stub construction and maintenance.
Mesquite Basin will construct the stub to the section and alignment shown on the approved Phase 2 improvement plans (compacted aggregate base with a bituminous surface course of the section noted on Sheet C-6). The stub will be barricaded at the Phase 3-side terminus with a Type III barricade and CCFD-compliant emergency-access knock-down gate. The stub will be maintained by Callaway for the duration of Phase 2 occupancy and until Phase 3 construction commences. Weekly inspection of the stub surface and barricade will be logged by Mesquite Basin during construction and by Callaway/HOA thereafter.
3.4  Signage.
"Emergency Access Only — No Public Through-Access" signage will be posted at the stub in both directions, per CCFD sign schedule. Contractor construction-access signage will be posted separately during the construction period only.
4.  BMP Installation Sequence per SWPPP
The project Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP), as authored by Sundial and covered under the NDEP General Permit NVR100000 Notice of Intent for Desert Sage Ranch, governs installation and sequencing of construction stormwater BMPs. The following sequence was walked and agreed on-site:
4.1  Prior to any grading disturbance.
The following perimeter and inlet-protection BMPs will be installed and inspected before any Phase 2 earthwork begins:
Silt fence and reinforced silt fence along the downgradient (south and west) perimeter of the Phase 2 disturbance area, as shown on the SWPPP site map.
Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad with wheel-wash provision) at the Rainbow Blvd. primary construction entry.
Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad) at the temporary stub terminus at Windmill Ln.
Inlet protection (sandbag berm or filter insert) at all existing off-site catch basins within 100 ft of the disturbance boundary along Rainbow Blvd. and Windmill Ln.
Concrete washout containment at the location shown on the SWPPP site map, off the primary construction entry.
Sundial's field engineer will walk the perimeter BMPs with Mesquite Basin's superintendent and sign the SWPPP inspection log the day the perimeter is complete and before earthwork disturbance begins.
4.2  During mass grading.
Track-out control at both construction entries will be inspected daily by Mesquite Basin and after each significant rainfall event. Wind-erosion control (application of water and, where directed, tackifier) will follow the schedule in the SWPPP and the requirements of the Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability dust control permit for the site.
4.3  As storm drain becomes operational.
As Phase 2 catch basins are installed, inlet protection (gravel bag or filter fabric type as noted in the SWPPP) will be placed at each basin the same day the frame and grate are set. Protection will remain in place until final stabilization or until paving is complete, whichever is later.
4.4  Stabilization.
Temporary stabilization of disturbed areas that will remain inactive for more than fourteen (14) days will be by application of tackifier or hydromulch, per the SWPPP. Final stabilization will be by landscape installation in improved areas and by soil binder / gravel treatment on Phase-2-facing slopes of the Phase 3 remainder that are disturbed by grading of the temporary stub.
4.5  Inspections and records.
Mesquite Basin will conduct SWPPP inspections weekly and within 24 hours after any rainfall of 0.25 inch or greater, log each inspection on the SWPPP inspection form, and correct deficiencies within the timeframes specified in the SWPPP. Sundial will spot-audit inspections at not less than a monthly interval. All SWPPP records will be kept at the site trailer and available for review by NDEP or Clark County inspectors.
4.6  Notice of Termination.
When Phase 2 improvements reach final stabilization and the improvements are accepted, Sundial will prepare and file a Notice of Termination with NDEP under NVR100000 to close construction stormwater coverage for the Phase 2 area of disturbance. The Notice of Termination will be limited to the Phase 2 area of disturbance and will be filed in the project record.
5.  Utility Coordination
5.1  Wet utilities.
Water.  Water main installation is by Mesquite Basin under LVVWD standard specifications, on the alignments and to the sizes shown on the approved plans. Pressure test and disinfection to LVVWD standards; LVVWD field acceptance required prior to service connection. LVVWD inspector to be scheduled by Mesquite Basin through the LVVWD construction desk with 48-hour notice.
Sewer.  Sewer main installation is by Mesquite Basin under CCWRD standard specifications. Mandrel test and low-pressure air test on completed reaches; CCWRD field acceptance required prior to backfill approval. Manhole vacuum test on all manholes. CCWRD inspection scheduled through CCWRD Plan Review Engineer's office (Vince Alarid, CCWRD).
5.2  Dry utilities (joint trench).
Composite dry utility plan (electric — NV Energy; gas — Southwest Gas; telecom — CenturyLink and Cox) is on file. Joint trench and conduit installation to be sequenced by Mesquite Basin after storm drain and sewer are backfilled and prior to base course. Each dry utility purveyor will inspect its own facilities prior to trench closure. The dry utility coordinator will attend a joint trench pre-installation meeting on-site before joint trench work begins; date to be set by Mesquite Basin.
5.3  Locating existing.
Blue-stake / USA North 811 will be called by Mesquite Basin for each work area 48 hours in advance of digging. Sundial will provide the contractor with the survey-verified locations of the offsite tie-ins at Rainbow Blvd.
5.4  Utility crossing conflicts.
Any utility crossing conflict identified in the field will be reported by Mesquite Basin to Sundial the same day. Sundial will provide a resolution or field revision within 24 hours where possible; where a field revision affects an approved plan sheet, Sundial will issue a numbered field revision memo and copy the County construction inspector.
5.5  Fire protection features.
Hydrant locations and fire department connections were walked by CCFD (Insp. Voight). Hydrant spacing on the plans meets CCFD standard. Hydrants are to be operational (flushed, tested, and flowed) prior to combustible construction commencing above the foundation on any dwelling unit. Hydrant flow test to be witnessed by CCFD and coordinated by Callaway's builder.
6.  Action Items Carried into Construction
The following action list was compiled at the close of the meeting. Owners are named.
End of Meeting Notes.

Las Vegas, NV 89103
(702) 555-0142  ·  NV COA #C-3874
Project: Desert Sage Ranch — Phase 3 Improvement Plans and Final Map
Sundial Project No.: 2201-03
Applicant / Owner: Callaway Land Partners
Pre-Application Meeting — Meeting Notes
Meeting date: 06/22/2026
Time: 10:00 a.m. – 11:20 a.m.
Location: Clark County Development Services, conference room (500 S. Grand Central Pkwy., Las Vegas)
Notes prepared by: Max Braddock, Project Manager, Sundial Engineering & Survey
Notes issued: 06/23/2026
1. Attendees
Callaway Land Partners was invited but did not attend; Max Braddock represented applicant-side coordination.
2. Purpose
Pre-application discussion of the Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 improvement plan and final map resubmittal package under the current code cycle. Objective was to align the design team and County reviewers on submittal composition, review path, and any threshold issues that ought to be flagged before intake, so the package can move through Public Works plan check on the first submittal without a routing surprise.
Phase 3 is the final 40.0 acres (60 half-acre lots) of the 140-acre subdivision entitled under Tentative Map TM-22-500041 (approved 03/14/2022). Phases 1 and 2 are built and occupied; the first final map in the series was recorded in 2024.
3. Topics Discussed
3.1 Submittal package composition and application numbers. Max walked through the intended package. County has already issued application numbers on the intake pre-check:
Improvement Plans: IP-26-100288
Final Map: FM-26-100290
Package as contemplated for first submittal:
Improvement plan set (grading, drainage, streets, wet/dry utility composite) — Sundial
Landscape and irrigation set — Ocotillo Landscape Studio
Final Map (three-sheet, second in the TM-22-500041 series) — Sundial Survey
Supporting reports: updated drainage narrative referencing the approved master drainage study; geotechnical addendum; traffic memo confirming trip generation is unchanged from tentative-map assumptions
Title report and closure package — Callaway to procure through Silver Butte Title & Escrow
Agency will-serve / capacity confirmations from LVVWD and CCWRD (see 3.5)
Dale Yeoman confirmed the two application numbers above are the correct references and should appear on the title block and cover sheets of every submitted sheet. He asked that IP-26-100288 be cited on the drainage narrative title page as well.
3.2 Drainage — master study governs. Priya summarized the drainage approach: Phase 3 drains to the detention basin sized under the approved master drainage study for the subdivision. Detention allocation for Phase 3 was fixed in that study; there are no departures anticipated in the resubmittal.
Dale confirmed that so long as the Phase 3 improvement plans match the volumes and outfall configuration in the district-approved master drainage study, no fresh hydrology submittal to Regional Flood Control is required — a narrative-level reconciliation in the drainage report is sufficient. He noted plan check will still verify the basin geometry against the study.
Priya to include a reconciliation table (basin volume as built into Phase 1/2, allocations for Phase 3, and headroom) in the drainage narrative.
3.3 Landscape — significant-change threshold. Bea Cortland summarized the landscape approach: streetscape palette carried forward from the approved 2022 Phase 1/2 palette (desert planting throughout streetscapes; turf confined to the HOA common-area park). Species list is substantially the same as Phase 1/2. Some substitutions in the shrub layer may be proposed as availability has shifted since 2022.
Odette Marchetti raised that any landscape changes from the approved 2022 palette may require review beyond staff level depending on extent — the significant-change threshold has to be evaluated on the actual proposed change. She referenced condition 14 of the tentative map approval letter, which contemplates design review as a public hearing before the Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission for significant changes to approved plans, including landscape and streetscape treatments in common areas.
Discussion did not resolve where the significant-change threshold sits for this project. Odette noted the evaluation is fact-specific and that the design team should provide a red-line comparison of the proposed Phase 3 palette against the 2022 approved palette so Planning can make that call once the actual proposed change is on paper. Bea agreed to prepare that comparison as part of the landscape resubmittal.
No commitment was made at the meeting as to whether the resubmittal will or will not trigger design review. The point was flagged for the team's awareness; a written determination from Planning would follow the submittal.
3.4 Fire access. Lt. Salazar (attending for Capt. Roark) noted that the CCFD review will focus on the permanent buildout access configuration for Phase 3. The temporary secondary access accepted at Phase 2 buildout was approved as a temporary condition pending Phase 3 development, and Phase 3 improvement plans need to show the permanent second point of access consistent with the tentative map. Any deviation from what was shown on TM-22-500041 should be pre-coordinated with Capt. Roark before submittal.
Sundial to circulate the current Phase 3 access layout to CCFD in advance of the formal submittal for informal review; the substantive determination on the permanent buildout condition will come from CCFD through the plan check letter.
3.5 Utilities. K. Odhiambo confirmed that separate confirmations from Las Vegas Valley Water District (LVVWD) and Clark County Water Reclamation District (CCWRD) will be needed for the resubmittal package. These are separate agency confirmations obtained by the applicant/engineer directly with each district; the County does not procure them.
Noted for the record; no further discussion.
3.6 SWPPP / grading permit sequencing. Priya asked about sequencing between improvement plan approval and the grading permit / SWPPP. Dale confirmed the standard sequence:
Improvement plans routed and approved (IP-26-100288)
NDEP Bureau of Water Pollution Control NOI filed by contractor; SWPPP prepared under NPDES general construction permit
Grading permit application submitted to Public Works with the SWPPP and approved improvement plans referenced
Grading permit issued once bonds/estimate are posted through Callaway
The grading permit cannot issue ahead of improvement plan approval. Dale mentioned that Callaway will need to have the surety and cost estimate lined up on the Public Works side before grading permit issuance, but that this is not a first-submittal item.
4. Agreed Submittal Route
The resubmittal will be routed through Clark County Public Works, Development Review, with Comprehensive Planning coordination on the landscape and final map conditions. Dale Yeoman is the assigned civil plans examiner (Public Works). Odette Marchetti is the point of contact on the Comprehensive Planning side for the tentative map conditions carry-forward and the significant-change evaluation.
Public Works will circulate the improvement plans internally to CCFD and Landscape review. Applicant is responsible for obtaining LVVWD and CCWRD confirmations separately (see 3.5) and including them in the submittal package.
Formal intake will be at the Public Works counter under application numbers IP-26-100288 (improvement plans) and FM-26-100290 (final map).
5. Action Items
End of notes. Distribute to attendees for correction; unless corrected within five business days, notes are the record of the meeting.
Max Braddock, PM
Sundial Engineering & Survey — NV COA #C-3874
4720 South Rainbow Boulevard, Suite 210, Las Vegas, NV 89103

 1. INTRODUCTION AND PROJECT DESCRIPTION
1.1 Purpose
The purpose of this Master Drainage Study is to establish the hydrologic and hydraulic basis of design for storm
drainage improvements serving the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision, a 140-acre residential development to be
constructed in three phases in the Enterprise area of unincorporated Clark County, Nevada. This study is
submitted to the Clark County Regional Flood Control District (CCRFCD) for acceptance and, upon acceptance,
is intended to serve as the master planning document governing all subsequent improvement plan submittals for
the individual phases.
1.2 Project Location
Desert Sage Ranch occupies a portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., in
unincorporated Clark County. The site is bounded generally by Rainbow Boulevard on the west and Windmill
Lane on the south, with the project address of record identified as Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las
Vegas, Nevada 89178. Assessor Parcel Number 177-27-201-001 encompasses the balance of the site not
already partitioned.
The site is located within the Enterprise Town Advisory Board area of unincorporated Clark County and is
governed by Clark County Code Title 30. Land use planning oversight is exercised by Clark County
Comprehensive Planning.
1.3 Site Description and Development
The 140-acre site is generally undeveloped desert terrain sloping gently from the northeast to the southwest at
an average grade of approximately 1.6 percent. Native ground cover consists of sparse creosote and bursage
on gravelly, well-drained soils overlying a caliche-influenced subsurface typical of the Enterprise sub-basin.
There are no defined natural watercourses across the site; historic runoff sheet-flows to the southwest.
Desert Sage Ranch will be developed as a single-family residential subdivision served by public streets. Phase
3 consists of 60 half-acre lots (100 ft × 220 ft, approximately 22,000 sf); Phases 1 and 2 consist of smaller
residential lots (approximately 6,050 sf, 55 ft × 110 ft) per the recorded Phase 1-2 Final Map. The full 140 acres
will be built out in three sequential phases:
 Phase 1 — 45.0 acres, northern portion of the site.
 Phase 2 — 55.0 acres, central portion of the site.
 Phase 3 — 40.0 acres, southern portion of the site, comprising 60 half-acre lots and associated street
frontage, HOA common-area park and streetscape improvements.
Each phase will be constructed under its own improvement plan set, prepared to be consistent with this Master
Drainage Study.

--- PAGE 3 ---
1.4 Regulatory Framework
This study has been prepared in conformance with:
 Clark County Regional Flood Control District Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual, edition
applicable at the time of preparation;
 Clark County Uniform Standard Drawings and applicable Public Works standards;
 Clark County Code Title 30 (development standards).
Hydrologic and hydraulic methods, precipitation input, loss rates and detention criteria are drawn from the
CCRFCD manual as it stood at the time of study preparation and acceptance. Subsequent phase-level design
shall comply with the master allocations set forth herein.
1.5 Study Deliverables
This document establishes:
 Design storm criteria and rainfall depths.
 Tributary-area delineation for the full 140 acres, broken down by development phase.
 Peak discharge estimates for the tributary sub-basins under fully developed conditions.
 A shared onsite detention approach with a fixed allocation of storage volume to each phase.
 Allowance for the full 140 acres at a shared outfall to the downstream regional facility, with a maximum
permitted discharge.
 A phasing exhibit identifying phase boundaries and detention basin locations.
 2. EXISTING CONDITIONS AND OFFSITE TRIBUTARY
2.1 Topography and Soils
Existing topography across the 140-acre site is a gently sloping desert plain. Elevations range from
approximately 2,905 feet at the northeast corner to approximately 2,850 feet at the southwest outfall point,
yielding an average site slope of approximately 1.6 percent to the southwest.
Surface soils across the site are classified as SM to SP-SM (silty sands and poorly graded sands with silt), with
cemented caliche horizons at variable depth. Infiltration rates in the caliche zone are low, and no percolation
credit is taken in the hydrologic analysis. The full computed runoff volume is treated as surface flow for the
purposes of this study.
2.2 Existing Drainage Pattern
Under existing conditions, stormwater sheet-flows overland from north-northeast to south-southwest across the
site. There are no defined channels within the property boundaries. At the southwest corner of the site, runoff

--- PAGE 4 ---
historically discharges toward the downstream regional drainage facility maintained by CCRFCD.
2.3 Offsite Tributary from the North
The site accepts a modest offsite drainage flow entering along the northern boundary of what will become Phase
1. The offsite tributary area upstream of the north boundary consists of approximately 38 acres of low-density
residential and open desert land. Under fully developed offsite conditions consistent with the surrounding land
use plan, the offsite peak inflow at the northern site boundary has been estimated as summarized in Section 3
and Appendix C.
The offsite tributary flow enters the site as sheet flow along the northern boundary and, at build-out, will be
conveyed through the Phase 1 street network to the shared onsite detention basin(s). No offsite bypass channel
is proposed; the accepted offsite flow is passed through the onsite storm drain and routed through detention
along with the onsite runoff.
2.4 Downstream Conveyance
The shared onsite outfall is located at the southwest corner of the property and discharges to the downstream
regional CCRFCD facility via an existing reinforced concrete pipe stub set during earlier regional construction.
The receiving facility has been reviewed against the shared outfall allowance identified in Section 5; downstream
capacity is not the controlling constraint for the site's release rate. The controlling constraint is the outfall
allowance established for Desert Sage Ranch and set forth in this study.

3.1 Design Storm

Manual applicable at the time of preparation. The following storms have been evaluated:
 100-year, 6-hour storm — used for peak discharge estimation and storm drain sizing.
 100-year, 24-hour storm — used for detention basin sizing (governing storage volume).

3.2 Method
Rainfall-runoff modeling was performed using CCRFCD-accepted methods appropriate for a subdivision of this
size, applying the Green-Ampt infiltration approach for pervious surfaces and directly-connected impervious
modeling for developed areas. Sub-basin delineation follows the tributary breakdown described in Section 3.3.

3.4 Peak Discharge Summary — Fully Developed Conditions
Fully developed peak flows to the shared onsite detention basin(s), computed under the 100-year, 6-hour storm
inclusive of the accepted offsite tributary inflow at the northern boundary, are summarized in Appendix C. The
peak inflow at the shared basin(s) governs the storm drain sizing but does not govern the shared outfall release,
which is fixed by the allowance in Section 5.
 4. DETENTION SIZING
4.1 Shared Onsite Detention Approach
Desert Sage Ranch is served by a shared onsite detention approach: the detention volume required to attenuate
the site's peak discharge to the accepted outfall release rate is provided in shared onsite detention facilities

--- PAGE 6 ---
constructed as the subdivision phases advance. Detention basin locations are identified on the phasing exhibit
(Section 6).
The shared approach avoids duplication of small phase-scale basins and consolidates operations and
maintenance for the HOA. Because the phases share the same outfall and downstream facility, the storage
requirement has been determined for the fully developed 140-acre site and then allocated among the three
phases in accordance with the acreage and impervious cover of each phase.
4.2 Governing Design Storm
Storage sizing is governed by the 100-year, 24-hour design storm. The 100-year, 6-hour storm is used to check
peak discharge to the shared basin(s) and storm drain sizing, but does not govern storage. Storage-indication
routing under the 100-year, 24-hour storm, with the outfall released at the allowance identified in Section 5,
produces a total site-wide required storage volume of 16.4 acre-feet.
4.3 Detention Allocation by Phase
Total storage required for the fully developed 140-acre site is allocated to the three phases on the basis of
tributary runoff volume and position in the shared outfall, not by pro-rata acreage. Phase 3 discharges last
and carries the largest attenuation duty; volumes were reviewed and fixed at District acceptance, and are

import openpyxl

def dump_sheet(p, sname):
    print("==========================================")
    print("XLSX:", p, "SHEET:", sname)
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(p, data_only=False)
    wb_val = openpyxl.load_workbook(p, data_only=True)
    ws = wb[sname]
    ws_val = wb_val[sname]
    for r in range(1, ws.max_row+1):
        row_vals = []
        has_content = False
        for c in range(1, ws.max_column+1):
            f_val = ws.cell(r, c).value
            v_val = ws_val.cell(r, c).value
            if f_val is not None or v_val is not None:
                has_content = True
            if isinstance(f_val, str) and f_val.startswith("="):
                row_vals.append(f"{v_val} [{f_val}]")
            else:
                row_vals.append(v_val)
        if has_content:
            print(f"R{r:02d}:", row_vals)

==========================================
PDF: /filesystem/Reports-Studies/DSR_Geotechnical_Report.pdf
--- PAGE 2 ---
We appreciate the opportunity to be of service on this project. Please contact the undersigned at (702) 555-0821
with any questions.
Respectfully submitted,
BIGHORN GEOSCIENCES INC.
Halston T. Cavender, P.E., G.E. Senior Geotechnical Engineer NV P.E. #16204
Attachments: Report body, figures, appendices
 Table of Contents
Executive Summary
Site Description
Field Investigation Program
Laboratory Testing Summary
Infiltration Testing
Engineering Recommendations
Boring Location Plan (Figure 2)
Limitations
Appendices
 Appendix A: Boring Logs BH-01 through BH-24
 Appendix B: Laboratory Test Results
 Appendix C: Infiltration Test Data Sheets
 Appendix D: Figures
 1. Executive Summary
This Geotechnical Investigation was performed at the proposed Desert Sage Ranch residential subdivision, a
140 acres master-planned community to be developed by Callaway Land Partners in three sequential phases
(Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3) within unincorporated Enterprise, Clark County, Nevada. The site is bounded
generally by Rainbow Boulevard to the west and Windmill Lane to the south, with undeveloped and partially
developed parcels to the north and east.
The subsurface exploration program consisted of twenty-four (24) hollow-stem-auger borings drilled between
September 13 and September 24, 2021, ranging in depth from 21.5 to 30.0 feet below existing grade, distributed
as approximately eight borings within each phase area. Six (6) infiltration tests were performed at basin-invert
candidate elevations to support drainage design. Selected samples were subjected to laboratory testing
including moisture-density, mechanical grading, Atterberg limits, expansion index, and soluble
sulfate/chloride/resistivity/pH corrosivity screening.
Key findings:

--- PAGE 3 ---
 Native soils across the site consist predominantly of Holocene alluvial fan deposits mapped as silty sand
(SM) and clayey sand (SC), grading with depth into weakly to strongly cemented caliche horizons typically
encountered between 4 and 8 feet below existing grade.
 Below the caliche horizon, dense to very dense silty sand with gravel and cobbles was encountered to the
maximum depths explored.
 Groundwater was not encountered in any boring to a depth of 30 feet. Historically high groundwater is
estimated to be more than 100 feet below existing grade in this portion of the valley.
 Expansion indices are low (EI < 20 on all samples tested); the surficial soils are non-expansive.
 Corrosion screening indicates the native soils are moderately corrosive to buried ferrous metals and
negligibly corrosive to concrete.
 Infiltration rates measured across six test locations range from 1.8 to 6.2 inches per hour in the upper silty
sand horizon and are considered favorable for surface retention/detention basin infiltration provided any
indurated caliche crust at the basin invert is over-excavated and replaced with select granular material.
The site is considered suitable for the proposed single-family residential development from a geotechnical
standpoint. Conventional spread footings founded on properly prepared and compacted engineered fill are
recommended for support of the residential structures. Pavement sections are provided herein for light-duty
residential streets and heavy-duty collector streets.
The following sections and appendices provide the detailed basis of these conclusions.
 2. Site Description
2.1 Location and Setting
The Desert Sage Ranch site occupies approximately 140 acres in Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60
East, Mount Diablo Meridian, within the Enterprise planning area of unincorporated Clark County, Nevada. The
property is bounded by Rainbow Boulevard on the west, Windmill Lane on the south, existing single-family
residential to the east, and vacant county-owned land to the north.
The site lies at the southern margin of the Las Vegas Valley on gently sloping alluvial fan deposits shed from the
Spring Mountains to the west. Ground surface slopes generally from northeast to southwest at approximately
1.5 to 2.5 percent. Site elevation ranges from approximately 2,895 feet at the northeast corner to approximately
2,848 feet at the southwest corner (NAVD88).
2.2 Existing Conditions
At the time of our field reconnaissance (September 8, 2021), the site was undeveloped and vegetated with
sparse Mojave Desert scrub — predominantly creosote bush (Larrea tridentata), white bursage, and scattered
Mojave yucca. Two informal dirt access roads traverse the northern portion of the property. No standing water,
seeps, springs, or evidence of prior ponding was observed. Isolated debris piles (household dumping) and
cattle-trail impressions are present near the northern boundary. There is no evidence of prior structural
development, agricultural cultivation, mining, or hydrocarbon storage on the property.
Well-developed desert pavement with pedogenic caliche fragments at surface confirms the geomorphic stability
of the site over the Holocene.

--- PAGE 4 ---
2.3 Adjacent Development
 West (across Rainbow Boulevard): existing single-family subdivisions constructed 2005–2012; typical
grade at right-of-way approximately at the same elevation as the western site boundary.
 South (across Windmill Lane): mixed commercial and an existing planned unit development; storm drain
outfall to an existing regional flood control channel is located approximately 1,400 feet east of the site along
Windmill Lane.
 East: two-acre custom-home parcels developed on private wells and septic prior to sewer extension; those
parcels have since been connected to sanitary sewer.
 North: undeveloped Clark County holding; a Bureau of Land Management right-of-way corridor for a
buried natural-gas transmission line crosses approximately 350 feet north of the site's north boundary.
2.4 Proposed Development
Callaway Land Partners has identified a three-phase build-out:
 Phase 1 — approximately 45 acres, northern portion of the site, single-family residential lots at
approximately 4 dwelling units per acre, with a central HOA park parcel and streetscape treatments.
 Phase 2 — approximately 55 acres, central portion of the site, single-family residential with a secondary
access to Rainbow Boulevard.
 Phase 3 — approximately 40 acres, southern portion of the site, half-acre single-family residential lots (60
lots) with common-area park and entry feature.
Improvements will include public and private streets, storm drainage with surface retention/detention basins,
sanitary sewer, water and dry utilities, and site landscaping.
 3. Field Investigation Program
3.1 Boring Layout
Twenty-four (24) exploratory borings, designated BH-01 through BH-24, were advanced across the site to
characterize subsurface conditions in each of the three planned phase areas. Approximate distribution:
 Phase 1 area (northern): BH-01 through BH-08 (8 borings)
 Phase 2 area (central): BH-09 through BH-16 (8 borings)
 Phase 3 area (southern): BH-17 through BH-24 (8 borings)
Boring locations were selected to provide coverage of each phase area, with additional borings located at
candidate detention/retention basin locations and along projected right-of-way alignments. Approximate boring
locations are shown on Figure 2, Boring Location Plan, with phase boundaries overlaid.
3.2 Drilling and Sampling

--- PAGE 7 ---
4.5 Corrosivity Screening
Four bulk samples were tested for corrosivity parameters. Results are summarized below.

Recommendations for concrete mix design and corrosion protection are provided in Section 6.
 5. Infiltration Testing
5.1 Test Locations and Methods
Six (6) surface/near-surface infiltration tests, designated INF-1 through INF-6, were performed at proposed
detention/retention basin locations. Testing was performed using the double-ring infiltrometer method (ASTM
D3385) at the anticipated basin-invert elevation, following removal of loose surficial materials and pre-soaking to
establish steady-state conditions. Where an indurated caliche crust was present at the intended test depth, a
test pit was excavated 12 inches into the underlying granular material and testing was performed on the
exposed sand layer, with a supplemental test performed on the caliche itself for comparison.

5.3 Interpretation
Measured infiltration rates in the shallow silty sand horizon (1.8 to 6.2 in/hr) are considered favorable for basin
infiltration and would support surface retention/infiltration basin design where the basin invert is established
either above the caliche horizon or where any indurated caliche crust encountered at the invert is
over-excavated (typically 12 to 24 inches) and replaced with clean, well-graded select granular material
(sand-and-gravel mixture with less than 10% fines).
Cemented caliche encountered at INF-4 is largely impermeable (0.2 in/hr) and is a limiting layer where present
at the invert. For final drainage design, we recommend a factor of safety of 2 applied to the field-measured
infiltration rate consistent with Clark County Regional Flood Control District guidance for infiltration-supported
detention/retention.
Complete infiltration test data sheets are provided in Appendix C.
 6. Engineering Recommendations
6.1 General
The site is considered suitable for the proposed single-family residential development from a geotechnical
standpoint provided the recommendations contained herein are incorporated into project design and
construction.
6.2 Site Preparation and Earthwork
Strip and remove all surface vegetation, root mats, debris and any topsoil pockets. Anticipated stripping
depth is generally less than 6 inches across the site.
Following stripping, the exposed subgrade shall be scarified to a depth of 8 inches, moisture-conditioned to
within ±2% of optimum moisture content, and compacted to a minimum of 95% of the maximum dry density
determined by ASTM D1557.
Engineered fill shall be placed in lifts not exceeding 8 inches loose thickness, moisture-conditioned, and
compacted to a minimum of 95% of the ASTM D1557 maximum dry density.
On-site native soils, free of oversized materials (particles greater than 4 inches in maximum dimension) and
organics, are suitable for reuse as engineered fill.
Over-excavation of localized caliche crust may be required at grade transitions to establish a uniform
subgrade support condition, particularly under building pads and pavements. Where cuts expose caliche
within 12 inches of finished subgrade, we recommend over-excavation to at least 24 inches below finished
subgrade and replacement with properly compacted engineered fill.
6.3 Foundation Recommendations
Conventional continuous and isolated spread footings founded on a minimum of 24 inches of properly
compacted engineered fill, or on native soils prepared as described above, are recommended for support of the
single-family residential structures.

--- PAGE 9 ---
 Allowable bearing pressure: 2,500 psf for dead-plus-live loads, increaseable by one-third for transient
loads (wind, seismic).
 Minimum footing width: 12 inches (continuous), 24 inches (isolated).
 Minimum embedment: 18 inches below lowest adjacent finished grade.
 Estimated total settlement: less than 1 inch; differential settlement less than ½ inch between adjacent
footings.
 Lateral resistance: coefficient of friction µ = 0.40 between footing base and compacted engineered fill;
allowable passive equivalent fluid pressure = 300 pcf against footing sides and grade beams, neglecting the
upper 12 inches.
Because the surficial soils are non-expansive (Section 4.4), post-tensioned slab-on-ground foundations are not
required from an expansion standpoint but may be selected at the structural engineer's option.
6.4 Pavement Section Recommendations
Traffic Index (TI) values were selected in consultation with the project civil engineer for two anticipated service
classifications. Recommended pavement section designs are based on an assumed R-value of 40 for the
compacted subgrade native soils, subject to verification by R-value testing (ASTM D2844) prior to paving.

Section 3.2. Phasing. The Property is subject to development in three sequential phases:

Section 3.3. Annexation of Successive Phases. Declarant reserves the right, exercisable in its sole discretion

Section 3.4. Public Rights-of-Way. All streets, alleys, and other public rights-of-way depicted upon any Map

 ARTICLE IV. COMMON AREAS
Section 4.1. Establishment of Common Area. Declarant hereby establishes and dedicates for the common

of each applicable Map, all Common Area, in fee simple, free and clear of all monetary encumbrances other

Section 4.2. Parcel A — Common-Area Park. The parcel designated Parcel A on the First Final Map (and as

the entire street frontage of the Property, in the extent depicted upon the First Final Map and upon any
successive final map recorded for Phase 3.

PDF: /filesystem/Correspondence/Agency/TM-22-500041_Conditions_of_Approval_03142022.pdf
--- PAGE 1 ---
CLARK COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF COMPREHENSIVE PLANNING 500 South Grand Central Parkway, 1st
Floor P.O. Box 551741 · Las Vegas, Nevada 89155-1741 (702) 455-4314 · www.clarkcountynv.gov
March 14, 2022
Callaway Land Partners Attn: Land Development Division 8880 W. Sunset Road, Suite 400 Las Vegas, NV
89148
RE: NOTICE OF APPROVAL — TENTATIVE MAP Application No.: TM-22-500041 Project: Desert Sage
Ranch Location: Rainbow Blvd. & Windmill Ln., Enterprise (unincorporated Clark County) Assessor's
Parcel No.: 177-27-201-001 Legal Description: Portion of Section 27, T. 22 S., R. 60 E., M.D.M., Clark
County, Nevada Hearing Date: 03/14/2022
Dear Applicant:
 Recital of the Request
Callaway Land Partners has filed application TM-22-500041 seeking tentative map approval for the residential
subdivision known as Desert Sage Ranch, comprising 140 acres to be developed in three phases in the
Enterprise planning area of unincorporated Clark County. As presented, the tentative map lays out a total
build-out of the subdivision with the final 40-acre phase (Phase 3) proposed for sixty (60) half-acre single-family
residential lots served by internal public rights-of-way, a shared detention facility, a homeowners association
park parcel, and streetscape improvements consistent with the approved land use designation.
The tentative map was reviewed by the Enterprise Town Advisory Board on the date noted in the record, by staff
of this Department, and by the reviewing agencies identified below. The application was heard by the Clark
County Planning Commission on this date.
 Findings
Based on the record before it, and after receiving the recommendation of staff and the recommendation of the
Enterprise Town Advisory Board, the Planning Commission finds that:
The tentative map substantially conforms to the requirements of Chapter 30 of the Clark County Code (Title
30 — Unified Development Code) applicable to the property, subject to the conditions of approval set forth
herein.
The proposed subdivision is consistent with the goals and objectives of the adopted Enterprise Land Use
Plan and the Clark County Comprehensive Master Plan.
Public services and facilities, including water, sewer, storm drainage, fire protection, and access, are or can
be made available to serve the subdivision at the densities and configurations shown, subject to the
conditions herein.
The applicant has demonstrated the ability to comply with Nevada Revised Statutes ("NRS") Chapter 278,
including but not limited to NRS 278.360, quoted below.
 Approval

--- PAGE 2 ---
Based on the foregoing findings, the tentative map identified as TM-22-500041, Desert Sage Ranch is hereby
APPROVED, subject to the thirty-one (31) numbered conditions set forth on the pages that follow. Compliance
with each condition is a prerequisite to any subsequent action of this Department or any other reviewing agency,
including improvement plan approval and final map recordation. Conditions are grouped by the department that
imposed them. The full set is binding regardless of grouping.
 Statutory Presentation Requirements
The applicant's attention is directed to NRS 278.360, which governs the presentation of final maps in a phased
subdivision, the substance of which is summarised below:
"A final map presented for recordation as the first map in a series must be presented to the
governing body within four (4) years after the date of approval or conditional approval of the tentative
map. Each successive final map in the same series must be presented within two (2) years after the
date on which the immediately preceding final map is recorded. Failure to timely present a map
terminates all proceedings relating to the subdivision. The governing body may, upon written
application filed after the applicable period has expired, grant an extension of not more than two (2)
years."
The applicant is on notice that the four-year and two-year periods described above run from the events identified
in the statute, not from any calendar reference stated by staff. Extensions of not more than two (2) years may be
sought only by written application filed after the applicable period has expired, and are discretionary with the
governing body. Nothing in this letter, and no informal communication from staff, shall be construed to extend,
waive, or modify the statutory deadlines.
 CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL
A. Public Works — Development Review (Conditions 1 through 10)
Improvement plans for all phases shall be prepared by a professional engineer registered in the State of
Nevada in accordance with the Clark County Uniform Standard Specifications and Drawings for Public
Works Construction and the Clark County Design and Construction Standards, current edition at the time of
submittal.
A drainage study, prepared in accordance with the Clark County Regional Flood Control District Hydrologic
Criteria and Drainage Design Manual, shall be submitted with the first improvement plan submittal for each
phase and shall demonstrate conformance with all applicable accepted district studies. Any proposed
deviation from district-accepted parameters shall be resubmitted for district re-review prior to improvement
plan approval.
Right-of-way dedications and easements shown on the tentative map, including all public utility easements,
drainage easements, and non-vehicular access easements, shall be granted by the recorded final map for
the phase in which the affected area lies.
Full half-street improvements shall be constructed along all abutting collector and arterial streets adjacent to
the phase being platted, including curb, gutter, sidewalk, pavement, streetlights, signing and striping, in
accordance with the applicable cross-section.

--- PAGE 3 ---
Internal streets shall be constructed to Clark County local-street standards. Cul-de-sac dimensions,
knuckles, and turning radii shall satisfy the requirements of both Public Works and the Clark County Fire
Department.
Sight visibility triangles shall be shown on the improvement plans and the landscape plans at every
intersection and driveway. Landscaping, signage, and walls within the sight visibility zone shall comply with
Section 30.52.025 (Sight Zones) of the Clark County Code.
A traffic impact analysis shall be provided at the improvement plan stage for any phase, or portion of a
phase, whose lot count, trip generation, or access configuration differs from the assumptions used in the
tentative map traffic study. Off-site mitigation, if warranted, shall be constructed or bonded as a condition of
the applicable final map.
Prior to recordation of any final map, the applicant shall furnish a performance bond, cash-in-lieu, or other
security acceptable to the Director of Public Works in the full amount of the engineer's estimate of probable
cost of the public improvements associated with that phase.
Final acceptance of public improvements for each phase shall be by written notice of acceptance from the
Director of Public Works following completion of the two-year maintenance period and the punch-list walk.
Bond release, in whole or in part, shall be governed by the terms of the applicable security instrument and
shall not occur automatically.
Construction stormwater discharges shall be authorized under the current Nevada Department of
Environmental Protection general permit (NVR100000) prior to the commencement of grading. A Notice of
Intent shall be filed and a Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan implemented for the duration of
construction, and a Notice of Termination shall be filed upon final stabilization.
B. Clark County Fire Department (Conditions 11 through 13)
Fire apparatus access roads, hydrant locations, hydrant flow, and required fire flow shall be shown on the
improvement plans and shall comply with the International Fire Code as amended and adopted by Clark
County. Secondary emergency access shall be provided in accordance with the Fire Code, and any
secondary access designated as temporary shall be identified as such on the plans with the expiration event
stated.
Water mains and appurtenances serving fire hydrants shall be operational and accepted, and required fire
flow shall be demonstrated by flow test, prior to combustible construction on any lot within the affected
phase.
Street names, address ranges, and access gate details (if any) shall be submitted for Fire Department
review concurrently with the improvement plan submittal. Access codes to any gates restricting emergency
access shall be provided to the Clark County Fire Department and the Metropolitan Police Department prior
to activation.
C. Comprehensive Planning (Conditions 14 through 20)
Any significant change to approved plans, including but not limited to landscape and streetscape
treatments in common areas, shall be subject to design review as a public hearing before the
applicable Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission prior to staff-level action.
The final map(s) shall conform to the tentative map as approved, including lot count, lot geometry, phase
boundaries, public street alignments, common-area boundaries, and dedications. Modification to any of the

--- PAGE 4 ---
foregoing at the final map stage that is not the result of a routine survey adjustment shall be treated as a
significant change under Condition 14.
Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions (CC&Rs) establishing a homeowners association, defining
common-area maintenance obligations, and identifying the party responsible for ongoing maintenance of
streetscapes, park parcels, entry features, walls, and drainage facilities not accepted by the County, shall be
recorded concurrently with the final map for the applicable phase. A common-area maintenance exhibit shall
be attached to the CC&Rs.
All identification signage, entry monumentation, and community features shall be shown on the landscape
plans and shall be subject to Comprehensive Planning review prior to installation. Off-premise signage is
not authorized by this approval.
Lighting on streetscape, park parcels, and entry features shall be full cut-off and shall comply with the
outdoor lighting standards of the Clark County Code. Photometric plans shall be provided with the
improvement plan submittal for common-area lighting.
Model home complexes, sales trailers, and temporary construction offices are not authorized by this
approval. Separate permits shall be obtained through this Department prior to the establishment of any such
use.
This approval does not vest zoning, use, or development standards beyond those in effect on the date of
approval. Nothing herein exempts the applicant from compliance with subsequently adopted regulations that
apply to actions taken after the effective date of those regulations, including but not limited to landscape and
water conservation standards.
D. Utilities (Conditions 21 through 24)
A will-serve letter from the Las Vegas Valley Water District for domestic water and fire flow service to the
phase being platted shall be current at the time of final map recordation. The applicant shall be responsible
for maintaining currency of the will-serve; a lapsed will-serve shall be re-issued prior to recordation.
A capacity confirmation from the Clark County Water Reclamation District for wastewater collection and
treatment capacity for the phase being platted shall be current at the time of final map recordation. Sewer
capacity confirmations are issued by the District under a separate schedule from water will-serve letters and
are subject to their own expiration terms; the applicant is responsible for verifying currency independently.
Dry utility joint-trench alignment shall be coordinated with the electric, natural gas, and telecommunications
purveyors. A composite dry utility plan shall be submitted with the improvement plans, and joint trench
easements shown on the final map shall reflect the composite plan as coordinated.
Backflow prevention, meter sizing, and cross-connection control shall comply with the requirements of the
Las Vegas Valley Water District and the Southern Nevada Health District.
E. Landscape (Conditions 25 through 28)
Landscape and irrigation plans shall be prepared by a landscape architect registered in the State of Nevada
and shall comply with Title 30, Chapter 30.64 (Site Landscape and Screening Standards) of the Clark
County Code, including the street frontage tree standard, plant palette, and turf restrictions in effect at the
time of submittal.

--- PAGE 5 ---
Streetscapes and medians shall be planted with low-water, climate-adapted plant material in accordance
with the Southern Nevada Water Authority regional plant list. Turf shall not be installed within any
streetscape, median, or right-of-way, nor within ten (10) feet of any street or curb.
Landscape plans for any phase proposing turf shall comply with all applicable Title 30 turf-placement
standards in effect at the time of the landscape submittal. Documentation supporting compliance shall
accompany the landscape submittal.
An irrigation demand worksheet shall be submitted with the landscape plans, showing water application
rates by irrigation method, area by hydrozone, and total annual demand. The worksheet shall be updated to
reflect any revision to the planting palette prior to landscape approval.
F. Other Reviewing Agencies (Conditions 29 through 31)
Southern Nevada Health District: Approval of the sanitary sewer connection to the regional system, and of
any private on-site treatment, shall be obtained prior to combustible construction. The Health District's
certificate shall appear on the recorded final map.
Clark County Recorder / Clark County Surveyor: The final map shall be prepared in accordance with NRS
278.010 through 278.630 and the map checklist of the Clark County Surveyor. The Recorder's note required
by NRS 278.5695 (examination of subsequent changes by reference to the cumulative index) shall appear on Sheet 1.
Nevada Division of Water Resources: The Division's approval shall appear on the final map for each phase.
 Statutory Presentation Deadlines (Reminder)
As stated above under Statutory Presentation Requirements, the first final map in the series must be presented
within four (4) years after the date of approval or conditional approval of the tentative map, and each
successive final map in the same series must be presented within two (2) years after the date on which the
immediately preceding final map is recorded. Failure to timely present a map terminates all proceedings
relating to the subdivision. An extension of not more than two (2) years may be granted only upon written
application filed after the applicable period has expired. The applicant is directed to compute its own
presentation deadlines from the operative events identified in NRS 278.360.
 Notice of Appeal
Any person aggrieved by this decision may appeal to the Clark County Board of County Commissioners by filing
a written notice of appeal with the Department of Comprehensive Planning within ten (10) calendar days of the
date of this letter. Appeals must be accompanied by the applicable fee. If no appeal is filed within the ten-day
period, this decision becomes final.
 Department Contact
Questions regarding these conditions of approval, or requests for interpretation, should be directed to:
Odette Marchetti Principal Planner Clark County Department of Comprehensive Planning 500 South Grand
Central Parkway, 1st Floor Las Vegas, NV 89155 Direct: (702) 555-4155 Email:
odette.marchetti@clarkcountynv.gov

--- PAGE 6 ---
Sincerely,
(signed)
Odette Marchetti Principal Planner Clark County Department of Comprehensive Planning

| 1. Does the emergency spillway as drawn on Sheet C-9 hold up, and can we answer Comment G-4 with what is on the sheet today? | NO.

Sheet C-9 (and the matching callout on Sheet C-6) must be revised prior to resubmittal. | While the basin stage-storage elevations on Sheet C-9 (2,851.00 ft bottom, 2,857.91 ft 100-yr WSEL storing 6.40 ac-ft [exact 6.401474977043159 ac-ft], 2,858.50 ft spillway crest storing 7.12 ac-ft [exact 7.124279155188246 ac-ft], and 2,859.20 ft top of berm storing 8.02 ac-ft [exact 8.021455463728191 ac-ft]) match DSR_Master_Drainage_Study.pdf Appendix D-2 (Page 8) and DSR_Ph3_StormDrain_HGL.xlsx (Inputs Rows 38–40), Sheet C-9 fails on five specific defects: (a) Internal arithmetic contradiction: the Spillway Detail labels the 2,858.50 ft weir crest 0.71 ft (0.71') above the 2,857.91 ft 100-year WSEL, while Basin Note 5 on the same sheet states 0.60 ft (0.60'), whereas exact subtraction is 2,858.50 ft − 2,857.91 ft = 0.59 ft (plus 2,859.20 ft − 2,858.50 ft = 0.70 ft to top of berm = 1.29 ft total freeboard); (b) Missing freeboard dimensioning and missing spillway cross-section: missed during the 08/18/2026 QA/QC review (DSR_Ph3_QAQC_Checklist.xlsx, Tab 3 Items 27–29), which misidentified Section B–B/C-9 as a "Basin outlet swale section"; (c) Hydraulic undersizing of the drawn 20.0 ft weir length: at H_max = 0.70 ft (2,859.20 ft top of berm), a 20.0 ft broad-crested weir (C = 2.60 ft^(1/2)/s) passes only 30.45442496584035 cfs (35.13972111443117 cfs at C = 3.00 ft^(1/2)/s), failing both the clogged-outlet emergency design inflow of 88.4 cfs (overtopping the berm by 0.7244021294130647 ft at WSEL 2,859.924402129413 ft) and the net surcharge overflow of 46.9 cfs (88.4 cfs − 41.5 cfs primary release at 2,858.50 ft, overtopping the berm by 0.2334971564832651 ft) — requiring weir widening from 20.0 ft to 60.0 ft (L_min = 58.05396102481341 ft); (d) Downstream apron geometric conflict & missing SD-402 details: the 5.50 ft drop (2,858.50 ft to 2,853.00 ft) at the 3H:1V exterior berm slope requires 16.50 ft horizontal run (17.392527130926087 ft slope length) just to reach the berm toe, before the 15.00 ft level energy-dissipation apron at 2,853.00 ft; and (e) Missing Basin Summary Block (G-3) and multi-stage outlet weir callout. |
| 2. Do the revisions required to resolve Comment G-4 trigger an amendment to the accepted Master Drainage Study? | NO.
The Sheet C-9/C-6 revisions do not trigger an amendment or re-submittal of the accepted Master Drainage Study to CCRFCD. | Per Condition 2 of the CCRFCD Acceptance Letter (Correspondence/Agency/FCD_MDS_Acceptance_Letter.pdf, dated 02/28/2022, File No. MDS-21-0118), an amendment to DSR_Master_Drainage_Study.pdf (Rev. 1, 02/2022) is triggered only by an increase in impervious cover (> 42%), a change in phase boundary or tributary area (40.0 ac gross / 42.05 ac with adjacent half-ROW), a reduction in detention storage below the Phase 3 allocation (6.4 ac-ft required; 6.40 ac-ft provided at 2,857.91 ft), or an increase in shared southwest outfall peak discharge (> 78.0 cfs cap; 77.4 cfs routed composite peak; 27.9 cfs Phase 3 release).
