steps.message:
The engineering memorandum evaluating Clark County Public Works First-Review Comment **G-4** (and companion Comment **G-3**) on the Phase 3 Detention Basin Emergency Spillway on Sheet C-9 has been completed and saved to:

- **Deliverable Path**: `/filesystem/Memo_to_Callaway_Spillway_2026-10-31.docx` (dated `10/31/2026`, addressed to **Garrett Nokes, VP Land Development, Callaway Land Partners**, and **Lee Chastain, Callaway Land Partners**, prepared for the signature of **Max Braddock, Project Manager, Sundial Engineering & Survey**, with technical concurrence block for **Jonathan R. Kessler, P.E., Principal-in-Charge / Engineer of Record, Nevada P.E. No. 14203**).

---

### Summary of Committed Dispositions and Key Technical Results

#### 1. Does the Spillway as Drawn on Sheet C-9 Hold Up, and Can We Answer Comment G-4 with What Is on the Sheet Today?
- **Committed Disposition**: **NO.** The emergency spillway as drawn on Sheet C-9 of `Design-Drafting/Phase 3/DSR_Ph3_Improvement_Plans_C1-C9.pdf` (`IP-26-100288`, First Submittal dated `08/21/2026`) does not hold up, and Comment G-4 (`Correspondence/Agency/CC-PW_1stReview_Comments_10092026.pdf`, dated `10/09/2026`, by Dale Yeoman, P.E., `NV P.E. #17832`) cannot be answered with what is on Sheet C-9 today. Sheet C-9 (and matching callouts on Sheet C-6) must be revised prior to second submittal for five specific reasons:
  1. **Internal Freeboard Arithmetic Contradiction on Sheet C-9 (`0.71 ft` vs. `0.60 ft` vs. exact `0.59 ft`)**:
     - Across the governing records (`Reports-Studies/DSR_Master_Drainage_Study.pdf` Appendix D-2, Page 8; `DSR_Ph3_Improvement_Plans_C1-C9.pdf` Sheet C-6 & Sheet C-9 Storage Summary Table; `Reports-Studies/DSR_Ph3_StormDrain_HGL.xlsx` Tab `Inputs` Rows 38–40 and Tab `HGL Summary` Row 20), the Phase 3 detention basin control elevations are:
       - Basin bottom: `2,851.00 ft` NAVD 88 (`29,450 sf`, `0.00 ac-ft`, `0.0 cfs`).
       - `100-year, 24-hour` (`3.18 in.`) routed water surface elevation (WSEL): `2,857.91 ft` NAVD 88 (`52,250 sf`, flow depth `6.91 ft`, tabulated storage `6.40 ac-ft` / exact average-end-area cumulative volume `278,848.25 cu ft = 6.401474977043159 ac-ft`, matching the `6.4 ac-ft` Phase 3 allocation; primary outlet release `27.9 cfs`).
       - Emergency spillway weir crest (on east berm): `2,858.50 ft` NAVD 88 (`54,480 sf`, depth `7.50 ft`, tabulated incremental freeboard-reserve storage `0.72 ac-ft` / exact `31,485.35 cu ft = 0.7228041781450872 ac-ft`; tabulated cumulative storage `7.12 ac-ft` / exact `310,333.60 cu ft = 7.124279155188246 ac-ft`; primary outlet release `41.5 cfs`).
       - Top of berm: `2,859.20 ft` NAVD 88 (`57,180 sf = 1.31267217630854 acres ≈ 1.31 acres`, structural depth `8.20 ft`, tabulated incremental storage `0.90 ac-ft` / exact `39,081.00 cu ft = 0.8971763085399449 ac-ft`; tabulated total structural storage `8.02 ac-ft` / exact `349,414.60 cu ft = 8.021455463728191 ac-ft`).
     - By exact subtraction, the vertical offset from the `100-year` WSEL to the emergency spillway weir crest is `2,858.50 ft − 2,857.91 ft = 0.59 ft`, the clearance from the weir crest to the top of berm is `2,859.20 ft − 2,858.50 ft = 0.70 ft`, and total freeboard from the `100-year` WSEL to the top of berm is `2,859.20 ft − 2,857.91 ft = 0.59 ft + 0.70 ft = 1.29 ft` (exceeding the `1.00 ft` minimum required by the CCRFCD *Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual* [HCDDM] and `DSR_Master_Drainage_Study.pdf` Section 3.3, Page 3).
     - On Sheet C-9 as drawn, however, `Detail — Emergency Spillway (Weir)` erroneously labels the weir crest as `"0.71' above 100-yr WSEL"` (`+0.12 ft` subtraction error), while `Basin Notes` Note 5 on the same sheet states `"0.60' above 100-yr WSEL"` (`+0.01 ft` rounding error that makes `0.60 ft + 0.70 ft = 1.30 ft != 1.29 ft`).
  2. **QA/QC Checklist Omissions (`Design-Drafting/Phase 3/DSR_Ph3_QAQC_Checklist.xlsx`, dated `08/18/2026`, Tab 3 Items 27–29, initialled `PS`)**:
     - Item 29 verified only that the `2,858.50 ft` numeric callout matched between Detail 4/C-9 and Section A–A/C-9, failing to verify the `0.59 ft` / `0.70 ft` / `1.29 ft` arithmetic, failing to enforce Dale Yeoman's Phase 2 Comment `G-3` precedent (`Correspondence/Agency/CC-PW_Ph2_Comments_1st_2nd.pdf`, Page 1; `DSR_Ph2_Comment_Response_Matrix.xlsx`, Row 8) requiring explicit graphic freeboard dimensioning on the detail, and misidentifying `Section B-B/C-9` (the North–South Transverse Section of the basin) in Item 27 as a `"Basin outlet swale section"`, leaving Sheet C-9 without an emergency spillway cross-section.
  3. **Hydraulic Undersizing of the As-Drawn `L = 20.0 ft` Broad-Crested Weir ($Q = C \cdot L \cdot H^{3/2}$)**:
     - The governing Phase 3 `100-year, 6-hour` (`2.38 in.`) routed peak inflow to the Phase 3 detention basin is `88.4 cfs` (`DSR_Master_Drainage_Study.pdf` Table 3-1, App. C-2, App. D-1; `DSR_Ph3_Hydrology_Worksheet.xlsx` Tab `Peak Flows` Row 13; `DSR_Ph3_StormDrain_HGL.xlsx` Tab `HGL Summary` Row 18 Reach `R14`; unrouted sub-basin arithmetic sum `96.8 cfs` across sub-basins `3A = 23.8 cfs`, `3B = 29.6 cfs`, `3C = 25.5 cfs`, `3D = 17.9 cfs`).
     - At the maximum available weir head before overtopping the `2,859.20 ft` top of berm ($H_{\text{max}} = 2,859.20\text{ ft} - 2,858.50\text{ ft} = 0.70\text{ ft}$, $H_{\text{max}}^{3/2} = 0.5856620185738529\text{ ft}^{3/2}$), the as-drawn `L = 20.0 ft` wide by `W = 6.0 ft` broad-crested weir passes only `30.45442496584035 cfs` at the standard ACB broad-crested coefficient $C = 2.60\text{ ft}^{1/2}/\text{s}$ (`31.625749002988055 cfs` at $C = 2.70\text{ ft}^{1/2}/\text{s}$; `32.79707304013576 cfs` at $C = 2.80\text{ ft}^{1/2}/\text{s}$; `35.13972111443117 cfs` at $C = 3.00\text{ ft}^{1/2}/\text{s}$; and `36.15877302674968 cfs` at theoretical maximum $C = 3.087\text{ ft}^{1/2}/\text{s}$).
     - Passing `88.4 cfs` (clogged primary outlet condition) over a `20.0 ft` weir requires $H = 1.4244021294130647\text{ ft}$ at $C = 2.60\text{ ft}^{1/2}/\text{s}$ (WSEL `2,859.924402129413 ft`, overtopping the `2,859.20 ft` berm by `0.7244021294130647 ft`). Even with an unclogged primary outlet passing `41.5 cfs` at `2,858.50 ft` ($Q_{\text{net}} = 88.4\text{ cfs} - 41.5\text{ cfs} = 46.9\text{ cfs}$), a `20.0 ft` weir requires $H = 0.9334971564832651\text{ ft}$ at $C = 2.60\text{ ft}^{1/2}/\text{s}$ (WSEL `2,859.433497156483 ft`, overtopping the `2,859.20 ft` berm by `0.2334971564832651 ft`).
     - Widening the emergency spillway weir crest length along the east berm from `20.0 ft` to **`L = 60.0 ft`** (above the exact minimum $L_{\text{min}} = 58.05396102481341\text{ ft}$ at $C = 2.60\text{ ft}^{1/2}/\text{s}$ and $H = 0.70\text{ ft}$) provides a maximum non-overtopping capacity of `91.36327489752104 cfs` at `2,859.20 ft`, passing `88.4 cfs` at $H = 0.6847811196969833\text{ ft}$ (WSEL `2,859.184781119697 ft`, unit discharge $q = 1.4733333333333334\text{ cfs/ft}$, critical depth $y_c = 0.4069878556455265\text{ ft}$, critical velocity $V_c = 3.620091278947722\text{ fps}$) and passing `46.9 cfs` at $H = 0.4487786242737256\text{ ft}$ (WSEL `2,858.948778624274 ft`, `0.2512213757262744 ft` below top of berm).
  4. **Downstream Apron Geometric Conflict & Missing SD-402 Construction Details**:
     - Natural grade beyond the east berm toe is `2,853.00 ft` NAVD 88 (`5.50 ft` vertical drop from the `2,858.50 ft` weir crest; `6.20 ft` vertical drop from the `2,859.20 ft` top of berm). At the specified `3H:1V` (`33.33333333333333%`) exterior berm slope, descending `5.50 ft` requires a horizontal run of `3 × 5.50 ft = 16.50 ft` (inclined slope length $\sqrt{16.50^2 + 5.50^2} = \sqrt{302.50} = 17.392527130926087\text{ ft}$) just to reach the exterior berm toe at `2,853.00 ft`. A single `15.00 ft` horizontal dimension from the weir sill to `2,853.00 ft` would steepen the exterior embankment to `2.727272727272727H:1V` and leave `0.00 ft` of horizontal energy-dissipation apron at `2,853.00 ft`.
  5. **Companion Comment G-3 & Multi-Stage Primary Outlet Annotation**:
     - Sheet C-9 lacks the formal Basin Summary Block referencing `DSR_Master_Drainage_Study.pdf` (Rev. 1, `02/2022`) and must annotate the upper overflow weir window above `2,855.00 ft` on Detail 3/C-9 that reconciles the stage–discharge jump from `20.2 cfs` (`2,855.00 ft`) to `27.9 cfs` (`2,857.91 ft`) and `41.5 cfs` (`2,858.50 ft`) in `DSR_Master_Drainage_Study.pdf` Appendix D-2.

---

#### 2. Do the Revisions Trigger an Amendment to the Accepted Master Drainage Study?
- **Committed Disposition**: **NO.** Revising Sheet C-9 (and Sheet C-6) to resolve Comment G-4 (and Comment G-3) **does not trigger an amendment or re-submittal** of the accepted Master Drainage Study (`Reports-Studies/DSR_Master_Drainage_Study.pdf`, Rev. 1 dated `02/2022`, sealed `02/14/2022` by Jonathan R. Kessler, P.E.) to the Clark County Regional Flood Control District (CCRFCD).
- **Record Basis (`Correspondence/Agency/FCD_MDS_Acceptance_Letter.pdf`, dated `02/28/2022`, File No. `MDS-21-0118`, signed by Steven C. Parrish, P.E.)**:
  - **Condition 2** triggers an MDS amendment only if Phase 3 (a) increases imperviousness above `42%` (`42%` maintained across all 12 subwatersheds `SB-01` through `SB-12` in `DSR_Ph3_Hydrology_Worksheet.xlsx`), (b) alters the phase boundary or tributary area (`40.0 acres` gross / `42.05 acres` including `2.05 acres` of adjacent half-street ROW maintained), (c) reduces detention storage below the `6.4 ac-ft` allocation (`6.40 ac-ft` / exact `6.401474977043159 ac-ft` provided at `2,857.91 ft`), or (d) increases peak discharge at the shared southwest outfall (`78.0 cfs` cap; `77.4 cfs` routed composite peak; `27.9 cfs` Phase 3 release maintained).
  - **Condition 3** explicitly delegates final basin grading, `1.0 ft` minimum freeboard verification, emergency spillway capacity, and outlet structure detailing to Clark County Public Works civil improvement plan review.
  - **Mandatory File-Hygiene Directive**: MRO's preliminary internal spreadsheet `Reports-Studies/DSR_Ph3_Detention_Calc_prelim.xlsx` (`09/25/2026`, labeled `"PRELIMINARY — DO NOT SUBMIT"`, which tested `65%` impervious cover, `66.5 acres` tributary area, and `8.1 ac-ft` storage) must be retired and excluded from the submittal package so that unauthorized parameters are never introduced into the record.

---

#### 3. What Must the Emergency Spillway Detail and the Basin Notes Say on the Revised Sheet C-9?
- **Revised `Detail 4/C-9 — Emergency Spillway (Broad-Crested Weir & Downstream Apron)` and New `Section C–C — Emergency Spillway Profile Section (Scale: 1" = 10' H, 1" = 5' V)`**:
  - **Freeboard & Elevations**: Graphically dimension `100-yr, 24-hr WSEL = 2,857.91 ft`, `Emergency Spillway Weir Crest = 2,858.50 ft` (`0.59 ft` vertical clearance above 100-yr WSEL), `Top of Berm = 2,859.20 ft` (`0.70 ft` vertical clearance above weir crest; `1.29 ft` total freeboard above 100-yr WSEL $\ge 1.00\text{ ft}$ CCRFCD minimum), and `Natural Grade Beyond East Berm Toe = 2,853.00 ft` (`5.50 ft` drop from weir crest; `6.20 ft` drop from top of berm).
  - **Weir Crest Construction & Hydraulic Sizing Block**: `L = 60.0 ft` clear crest length along east berm (`2:1` side transition tapers to `2,859.20 ft`), `W = 6.0 ft` broad-crested sill width in direction of flow, surfaced with `12 in. × 18 in.` (`1.0 ft × 1.5 ft`) articulated concrete block (ACB) mat (`6 in.` / `0.50 ft` thick) over `8 oz/sy` nonwoven geotextile filter fabric and `6 in.` (`0.50 ft`) compacted Type II aggregate bedding, anchored by `24 in. deep × 12 in. wide` (`2.00 ft × 1.00 ft`) reinforced concrete sill cutoff keys ($f'_c = 4,000\text{ psi}$, `#4` rebar). State hydraulic capacity: $Q_{\text{max}} = 91.36327489752104\text{ cfs}$ (`91.4 cfs`) at $H_{\text{max}} = 0.70\text{ ft}$ ($C = 2.60\text{ ft}^{1/2}/\text{s}$); clogged-outlet design inflow $Q_{100} = 88.4\text{ cfs}$ passed at $H = 0.6847811196969833\text{ ft}$ (`0.68 ft`, WSEL `2,859.184781119697 ft` / `2,859.18 ft`, $y_c = 0.4069878556455265\text{ ft}$, $V_c = 3.620091278947722\text{ fps}$); unclogged surcharge overflow $Q_{\text{net}} = 46.9\text{ cfs}$ passed at $H = 0.4487786242737256\text{ ft}$ (`0.45 ft`, WSEL `2,858.948778624274 ft` / `2,858.95 ft`, residual freeboard `0.2512213757262744 ft` / `0.25 ft`).
  - **Downstream `3H:1V` Exterior Chute & `15.00 ft × 60.0 ft` Horizontal Apron**: Separate the `16.50 ft` horizontal run (`17.392527130926087 ft` / `17.39 ft` slope length) `3H:1V` exterior embankment chute ($y_n = 0.1850735853463120\text{ ft}$, $V_n = 7.960797253294476\text{ fps} < 15.0\text{ fps}$, $\text{Fr} = 3.2610190364709333$ at $n = 0.035$) from the `15.00 ft` long by `60.0 ft` wide horizontal energy-dissipation apron at `2,853.00 ft` ($y_2 = 0.7659852069351478\text{ ft}$, $L_{\text{jump}} = 3.485469729533015\text{ ft}$, exit velocity $V_2 = 1.923448809702819\text{ fps}$), both armored with `24 in.` (`2.00 ft = 2 × D50`) thick grouted rip-rap (`D50 = 12 in. / 1.00 ft`, min. specific gravity `2.65`, grout $f'_c = 3,000\text{ psi}$ filling `50%–65%` depth with `3 in.` PVC weep holes at `6.0 ft` O.C.) over `6 in.` granular bedding and nonwoven geotextile filter fabric with a `36 in. deep × 12 in. wide` (`3.00 ft × 1.00 ft`) concrete toe cutoff wall at the downstream end per Clark County Uniform Standard Drawing `SD-402` (total armored area `1,943.5516278555652 sq ft = 215.95018087284058 SY`, covered within the `500 SY` / `$43,000.00` Line `2.42` bid allowance in `Cost Estimates/DSR_Ph3_Engineers_Estimate.xlsx`).
- **Revised `Basin Notes` (Notes 1–6) and `Basin Summary Block` (Comment G-3)**:
  - Correct Basin Note 5 to state the exact `0.59 ft (0.59')` offset above the `2,857.91 ft` 100-year WSEL and `0.70 ft (0.70')` below the `2,859.20 ft` top of berm (`0.59 ft + 0.70 ft = 1.29 ft` total freeboard $\ge 1.00\text{ ft}$ minimum), together with the `L = 60.0 ft`, `W = 6.0 ft` weir dimensions, `88.4 cfs` / `91.4 cfs` hydraulic capacities, `3H:1V` exterior chute (`16.50 ft` horiz. / `17.39 ft` slope), `15.00 ft × 60.0 ft` horizontal grouted rip-rap apron (`D50 = 12 in.`, `24 in.` thick per `SD-402`) at `2,853.00 ft`, and downstream discharge pathway.
  - Add the boxed **Phase 3 Detention Basin Summary Block** citing the required `6.4 ac-ft` allocation, the `6.40 ac-ft` (`278,848.25 cu ft = 6.401474977043159 ac-ft`) provided at `2,857.91 ft` (`7.12 ac-ft` at `2,858.50 ft`; `8.02 ac-ft` at `2,859.20 ft`), and referencing *"Master Drainage Study for Desert Sage Ranch, Clark County, Nevada"* (Sundial Job No. `2201-01`, Rev. 1 dated `February 2022` / sealed `02/14/2022`, accepted by CCRFCD on `02/28/2022` under File No. `MDS-21-0118`).

---

#### 4. Where Does the Overflow End Up Once It Leaves the East Berm?
- **Committed Disposition**: Once emergency overflow leaves the east berm weir crest (`2,858.50 ft` NAVD 88), it follows a four-stage, fully contained surface pathway that bypasses all residential lots (`Lots 31–60`):
  1. **Down the `3H:1V` Armored Exterior Chute to the Horizontal Apron at Natural Grade (`2,858.50 ft` to `2,853.00 ft` NAVD 88)**: Flow descends the `5.50 ft` vertical drop (`16.50 ft` horizontal run / `17.392527130926087 ft` slope length) down the `3H:1V` grouted rip-rap exterior berm slope and traverses the `15.00 ft × 60.0 ft` horizontal grouted rip-rap energy-dissipation apron (`D50 = 12 in.`) to natural grade beyond the east berm at `2,853.00 ft` NAVD 88 (`DSR_Ph3_Improvement_Plans_C1-C9.pdf`, Sheet C-6 Page 12 & Sheet C-9 Page 17).
  2. **Through the Downstream Open Drainage Swale Within HOA Common-Area Parcel "E" (`2.04 Acres`)**: Exiting the apron toe cutoff wall at `2,853.00 ft` (`V_2 = 1.923448809702819 fps`), flow spreads into the downstream open drainage swale inside HOA-owned **Common-Area Parcel "E"** (`2.04 acres` per `Design-Drafting/Survey/DSR_Ph3_FinalMap_FM-26-100290_checkprint.pdf` Sheet 4 of 4 and `Tenders-Contracts/DSR_CCRs_CommonArea_Exhibit.pdf` Section 3.1, where the `57,180 sf = 1.31267217630854-acre` basin footprint leaves `0.72732782369146 acres [31,682.40 sf]` of common-area buffer and open swale corridor), keeping all overflow below adjacent residential pads (`2,856.00 ft` to `2,868.00 ft` in Subwatersheds `SB-11` and `SB-12` on Sheet C-7).
  3. **Exits at the Windmill Lane Curb-and-Gutter Line**: The Parcel "E" open swale discharges onto the existing **Windmill Lane gutter line** along the south boundary of Parcel "E" (`40.0 ft` half right-of-way with existing vertical curb and gutter; Sheet C-2 Page 4, Sheet C-6 Page 11, Sheet C-7 Pages 13–14, Sheet C-9 Page 17, and `DSR_Ph2_AsBuilts.pdf` Sheet RD-4 Tie-in `T-1`).
  4. **West Along Windmill Lane to the CCRFCD Regional Storm Drain Facility & Regional Flood Control Channel**: Flow travels west along the Windmill Lane north gutter following the `1.5% to 2.5%` northeast-to-southwest grade (passing the Desert Sage Parkway / Windmill Lane return low point at `Sta. 22+80`, gutter elevation `2,853.40 ft`, paired curb inlets `SD-INL-11` and `SD-INL-12` on Sheet C-7 Page 14) to the **Rainbow Boulevard / Windmill Lane intersection**, where it is captured by the **existing CCRFCD regional storm drain facility in Windmill Lane** (`DSR_Master_Drainage_Study.pdf` Sections 1.2, 3.2, 4.1 & Appendix A; `FCD_MDS_Acceptance_Letter.pdf` Page 1) and conveyed to the regional flood control channel (`Reports-Studies/DSR_Geotechnical_Report.pdf` Section 2.3, Page 4).
